candidates.hypothesis: 3rd Friday Price Spike (3FPS): on each monthly a.m.-settlement 3rd Friday, equity index futures drift up from Thursday close to the Friday 08:30 CT open (SOQ) and fully revert by about 11:00 CT (noon ET). Trade: long MES/MNQ in the Thursday night session, flat or reverse to short at the Friday open, cover by 11:00 CT or the Friday close.
candidates.mechanism: SOQ settlement of a.m. SPX/NDX/DJX options and futures; authors' preferred channel is dealer 'charm' hedging (option deltas drift as expiry nears, dealers buy into the SOQ), with immediacy/inventory reversal after the open; manipulation not excluded by the authors.
candidates.entry_window_ct: leg 1: Thursday 17:00 CT session reopen (Topstep cannot hold through 15:10-17:00 CT) to Friday 08:30 CT; leg 2: short Friday 08:30 CT to about 11:00 CT (paper: 'fully reverts afterward by about noon 3rd Friday') or Friday 15:00 CT close
candidates.hold: leg 1 about 15.5 h inside one Topstep trading day; leg 2 2.5 to 6.5 h
candidates.best_source: Baltussen, Terstegge, Whelan (2024), The Derivative Payoff Bias, working paper, version September 2024 (AEA 2025 program copy)
candidates.sample: S&P 500 E-mini futures trade prices and SPX index, 2003 to 2021 (about 228 monthly 3rd Fridays); NQ and YM shown in Figure 5 only (no table)
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: no hold-out; sample includes 2015-2021; 'present in almost every year since 2003'; no 2022+ (0DTE era) evidence in this version
candidates.published_effect: ES futures, Table II Panel (b): Thursday close to Friday open +14.30 bp (t 3.54, sd 60.53 bp); Friday open to Friday close -12.89 bp (t -2.40, sd 80.45 bp). Combined long-then-short trade (Table A.4): 27 bp mean at mid quotes, 24.20 bp after bid-ask (t 3.47, sd 104.60 bp, annualised SR 0.80 at 12 trades a year)
candidates.price_level_used: ES 6,000 (stated for conversion; ES traded about 5,500 to 6,700 in 2025-2026)
candidates.micro: MES (0.25 pt tick). Leg 1: 14.30 bp x 6000 / 10000 = 8.58 ES points / 0.25 = 34.3 MES ticks. Leg 2: 12.89 bp -> 7.73 points -> 30.9 MES ticks. Combined after spread 24.20 bp -> 14.52 points -> 58.1 MES ticks. NQ not tabulated: if NQ matched ES in bp, 14.30 bp x 21000 / 10000 = 30.0 NQ points = 120 MNQ ticks [assumption, not published]
candidates.gross_or_net: gross (legs, Table II); net of bid-ask only for the combined trade (Table A.4 Panel b), no commission
candidates.dispersion: leg 1 per-event sd 60.53 bp, t 3.54; leg 2 sd 80.45 bp, t -2.40; combined sd 104.60 bp, SR 0.80 (annualised over 12 holding periods)
candidates.quote_location: Table II p.41 (btw.txt lines 1893-1904); text p.12-13 (lines 505-563); Table A.4 Panel (b) (lines 3104-3121)
candidates.decay_evidence: Figure 4 Sharpe by year: 'The strategy earns positive returns in almost all years and annual Sharpe ratios that are generally large, with many exceeding 2.' No post-2021 data; the 0DTE shift to p.m. settlement since 2022 could weaken or strengthen it (authors: 0DTE options expire in the p.m. window). Unknown share of leg 1 accrues 15:00-17:00 CT Thursday, which Topstep cannot hold.
candidates.data_needed: 1-minute MES/MNQ/NQ bars (owned) and a monthly 3rd-Friday expiry calendar (derivable; quarterly dates fall in the roll blackout)
candidates.research_window_testable: partial (about 15 monthly 3rd Fridays 2025-04..2026-06, low power; 2022-2024 owned NQ/MES bars are post-sample for the paper)
candidates.why: Found by the KMW forward-citation dig (a later paper by co-author Whelan). Published per-event size is about 10x the MES hurdle (about 3 MES ticks) even after spread; fits Topstep's 17:00-15:10 CT trading day if leg 1 starts at the 17:00 CT reopen.
candidates.prop_notes: Leg 1 is held overnight but inside one Topstep trading day (17:00 CT Thu to 08:30 CT Fri); flat before 15:10 CT Friday. Not a scheduled news release (P06 not triggered unless a release coincides). 12 trades a year means a Combine cannot be passed on this alone and the consistency rule (best day < 55% of total) binds; only an add-on to a book. Quarterly 3rd Fridays coincide with the roll blackout.
candidates.overlap_note: DUPLICATE of R12-C1 (intraday leg) and R12-C2 (overnight leg): same paper, found independently here through the KMW forward-citation dig (co-author Whelan); RD4 adds no new numbers beyond R12, the lead should merge. E-H3 shorted quarterly witching 14:30-15:00 CT; 3FPS is the overnight run-up into the 08:30 CT SOQ and the morning reversal on all monthly 3rd Fridays. R1 (0DTE/dealer charm) may also own this paper; overlap with R1 unchecked.

evidence.claim: KMW reversals measured on CME futures (dollar portfolio) are smaller than spot for the post-London leg
evidence.number: post-L: spot 1.20 bp (t 3.08), CME futures 0.64 bp (t 2.20); pre-E: spot -1.65, CME -1.64 bp
evidence.location: Table III p.33 (columns pre-T post-T pre-E E-L post-L CTC); sample June 2006 to December 2019
evidence.source: Krohn, Mueller, Whelan (2024), Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock, Journal of Finance 79(1); WRAP copy (version January 2023)

evidence.claim: KMW: a liquidity-demanding trader loses money on the fix reversals after costs
evidence.number: AUD LD pre-L+post-L -6.53 bp (t -5.86); GBP -0.73 bp (t -0.74)
evidence.quote: for the trader (or liquidity demander), reversal returns turn negative once transaction costs are taken into account. Thus, the unconditional return patterns cannot easily be arbitraged away by traders that seek to exploit the intraday reversals.
evidence.source: Krohn, Mueller, Whelan (2024), Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock, Journal of Finance 79(1); WRAP copy (version January 2023)

evidence.claim: KMW: downward trend in reversal returns at the end of the sample
evidence.quote: While the reversal returns are mostly positive, we do observe a downward trend towards the end of the sample period ... arbitrage capital is indeed allocated to exploiting the reversal patterns, leading to a decline in the intraday return predictability.
evidence.source: Krohn, Mueller, Whelan (2024), Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock, Journal of Finance 79(1); WRAP copy (version January 2023)

evidence.claim: Osler-Turnbull: fix price dynamics qualitatively unchanged since 2015 (theory; their own data end 2013)
evidence.quote: Our model can explain why fix-price dynamics are qualitatively unchanged since 2015 despite notable reforms (Ito and Yamada, 2017b; van der Linden, 2017)
evidence.location: section B Fix regulation (txt line 1910); data: 'Data for all currencies end in December 2013' (line 1644)
evidence.source: Osler, Turnbull, Dealer Trading at the Fix, Brandeis WP 101R (published as Dealer misconduct and price dynamics at the fix, JBF 185, 2026)

evidence.claim: Ito-Yamada: post-reform month-end contrarian EUR/USD after spread
evidence.number: +1.21 bp (15 min), +1.32 bp (5 min), -1.02 bp (1 min); intra-month negative
evidence.quote: After Reform, End of month: 'EUR/USD ... 1.21 1.32 -1.02' ... After Reform, Intra month: 'EUR/USD -0.519 -0.395 -0.861' [E.0 verified passage P-K3-002-g]
evidence.location: Table 2 (via E.0 notes lines 145-150); NBER copy not refetched (NBER terms forbid automated access)
evidence.source: Ito, Yamada (2017/2018), Did the reform fix the London fix problem?, JIMF 80; NBER w23327 [secondary-only: E.0 reader's verified quote]

evidence.claim: Evans et al. (FCA 2018): short-term reversals around the fix disappear from 2015
evidence.quote: We find that short-term price reversals in prices around the fix decrease steadily throughout our sample period, and disappear from 2015 onwards. [E.0 verified passage P-K3-019-a]
evidence.location: FCA OP46 summary (via E.0 notes line 376)
evidence.source: Evans, O'Neill, Rime, Saakvitne (2018), FCA Occasional Paper 46 [secondary-only: E.0 reader's verified quote]

evidence.claim: Evans (2018) month-end strategy returns are annualised daily means (x252 convention); per-event size ambiguous
evidence.number: EUR/USD 3.965 'annual percent' at 1 min: about 1.57 bp per event if x252, about 33 bp if x12
evidence.quote: Because returns are generated at the daily frequency, I include the 1/sqrt(252) scale factor to 'annualize' the ratio (using the convention that a year equals 252 trading days).
evidence.source: Evans (2018), Forex trading and the WMR Fix, JBF 87 (MPRA 81583)

evidence.claim: Price-limit continuation is concentrated in the close-to-open gap, not the next day's session
evidence.quote: a 1% increase in the return calculated from limit day close to options-implied prices is associated with a 0.76% increase in the close-to-open futures returns, and 0.15% increase in the close-to-close futures returns. Implied prices forecast next day opening prices better than closing prices
evidence.source: Janardanan, Qiao, Rouwenhorst, On commodity price limits, WP Feb 2017 (JFM 39(8) 2019)

evidence.claim: After a locked-limit day lean hogs/live cattle gap beyond the limit at the open and then hold the level for the first hour
evidence.number: gap 0.3 to 0.4 c/lb beyond the previous limit (median)
evidence.quote: On the next trading day following a locked-limit day, the price jumps to a new level that is 0.3 to 0.4 cents/lb. outside the previous day's limit. The price level remains persistently far from the previous limit after one hour of trading
evidence.location: printed p.69 (txt lines 3213-3223); Figure 3.1 note p.84; sample 6 June 2014 to 23 December 2019
evidence.source: He, X. (2022), Essays on extreme events in agricultural futures markets, PhD dissertation, University of Illinois, ch.3

evidence.claim: Temporary-limit moves reverse, but the temporary/locked split is defined ex post (whether the limit lasts to the close)
evidence.number: post-limit level about 0.5 c/lb inside the range (median); 144 HE temporary vs 172 locked events
evidence.quote: When the last limit move continues until the end of the trading session, we characterize the corresponding event as a locked-limit day, otherwise, we characterize the event as a temporary limit day.
evidence.source: He, X. (2022), Essays on extreme events in agricultural futures markets, PhD dissertation, University of Illinois, ch.3

evidence.claim: WASDE soybean reaction grows from 30 min to the close, but needs analyst-surprise data and the increment is about 1.3 standard errors

evidence.number: +14.30 bp Thu close to Fri open; -12.89 bp Fri open to close; 24.20 bp combined after spread
evidence.quote: The average overnight cumulative return in the active futures contract is equal to 14 bps which completely reverses by 12:00.
evidence.location: p.12 (txt lines 505-513); Table II; Table A.4
evidence.source: Baltussen, Terstegge, Whelan (2024), The Derivative Payoff Bias, working paper, version September 2024 (AEA 2025 program copy)
